Exploring Economic and Social Conditions Across the U.S. Counties

Data

Data Source: The data used in this analysis and visualizations come from the ‘Urban Institute’s Upward Mobility Framework’. The data set showcases longitudinal county-level measures related to economic and social conditions in relation with upward mobility in the US. (URL:https://datacatalog.urban.org/dataset/mobility-metrics-data-upward-mobility-framework)

options(scipen = 999)

# Loading the necessary packages
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

# Loading the data into folder using Assingment02 method
mobility_link <-
  paste0("https://urban-data-catalog.s3.amazonaws.com/drupal-root-live/2026/06/03/11_mobility-metrics_county_longitudinal.csv")

if (!file.exists("11_mobility-metrics_county_longitudinal.csv")) {
  
  download.file(mobility_link,
                 destfile = "11_mobility-metrics_county_longitudinal.csv")
} 

# Loading the data into the global environment
mobility <- read_csv("11_mobility-metrics_county_longitudinal.csv")

# Taking a glimpse into the data
glimpse(mobility)

Visualization 1 - Changes in Employment Across U.S. Counties

# Filtering NAs from the variable 'share_employed', calculating the mean by 
# year and visualizing the average employment share over time 
mobility |>
  filter(!is.na(share_employed)) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarize(
    mean_share_employed = mean(share_employed)
  ) |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = year, y = mean_share_employed)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent()
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 2014:2024
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Employment Share Across U.S. Counties",
    subtitle = "Unweighted mean county employment share, 2014-2024",    
    x = "Year", 
    y = "Average employment share",
    caption = "Source: Urban Institute, Upward Mobility Framework. No data available for 2020" 
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

Interpretation: The average employment share across U.S. counties increased from ~76% in 2014 to >80% in 2024. The increase remains relatively consistent until 2019, followed by a lower share in 2021 and renewed increase until 2024. Since the measure captures an unweighted county average, the visual highlights changes in the average rather than the employment share of the total U.S. population. While it suggests an improving employment siutation, it cannot explain whether these opportunities are distributed evenly across counties.

Visualization 2 - Differences in Household Income Across U.S. Counties

# Filtering for 2024 and non-missing pctl_income_50 values and visualizing
# the distribution of household incomes across U.S. counties
mobility |>
  filter(year == 2024,
         !is.na(pctl_income_50)
         ) |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = pctl_income_50)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5000, fill = "orange") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Household Income Across U.S. Counties",
    subtitle = "Household income at the 50th percentile, 2024",
    x = "Household income at the 50th percentile (USD)",
    y = "Number of counties",
    caption = "Source: Urban Institute, Upward Mobility Framework." 
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

Interpretation: In 2024, household income varied considerably across U.S. counties, while the histogram suggests most counties being concentrated around the middle of the distribution at around 60-70k. Importantly, the distribution is right-skewed, with a small number of counties showcasing a substantial higher 50th-percentile household income compared to most other counties. Even though having seen the first visualization of the overall improvement in employment, this histogram suggests that economic conditions differ considerably across counties. These geographic differences suggest that general national trends alone may hide important differences in local economic opportunities for citizens.

Visualization 3

mobility |>
  filter(
    year == 2024,
    !is.na(share_employed),
    !is.na(pctl_income_50)
  ) |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = share_employed, y = pctl_income_50)) +
  geom_point(mapping= aes(size = population), alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent()
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Employment and Household Income Across U.S. Counties",
    subtitle = "Employment-to-population ratio and 50th-percentile household income, 2024",
    x = "Employment-to-population ratio (ages 25-54)",
    y = "Household income at the 50th percentile (USD)",
    caption = "Source: Urban Institute, Upward Mobility Framework" 
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
